 Nebraska Wesleyan to Offer Student Loan Repayment Help Starting in Fall 2027
 By Johnnie Adcox 
 Nov 19, 2026 | 2:51 PM 
 Nebraska Wesleyan University will offer incoming undergraduates help repaying student loans after graduation if they earn less than $60,000 a year. The program starts with first-year and transfer students entering in fall 2027, and families can sign up at no cost.
 To qualify for reimbursement, students must opt in, graduate from Nebraska Wesleyan, work at least 30 hours a week and begin making loan payments. The program covers eligible federal student loans, parent PLUS loans and private education loans.
 Tom Ochsner, Nebraska Wesleyan’s director of scholarships and financial aid, tells KLIN News that graduates make their regular loan payments and receive any reimbursement “once a quarter.” He said the amount varies based on the graduate’s income and payments on eligible debt.
 Ochsner said the university wants graduates to be able to consider jobs that might pay less, such as positions at nonprofits, while keeping up with their loans. “It’s really just a safety net that we’re trying to provide for them to be able to do that,” he said.
 Nebraska Wesleyan is working with Ardeo Education Solutions to administer the program. Incoming students can accept the offer through Ardeo, submit their enrollment deposit and enroll at Wesleyan. The university has yet to set a sign-up deadline, Ochsner said. Enrollment details are available on Nebraska Wesleyan’s loan repayment assistance page .
